title: An event planner
description:
Build a command-driven event planner. It reads one command per line until `quit` or the end of the input, keeps a schedule, refuses overlapping events, and finds free time. Commands are parsed by `Command.parse` from practice 6.05, which is already in the project (`Command.java`). The program is four files: `Main.java` (the command loop), `Event.java`, `Schedule.java` and `Command.java`.

```
add 2026-03-14 09:00 90 Team meeting
add 2026-03-14 12:00 60 Lunch
add 2026-03-14 10:00 30 Call
day 2026-03-14
free 2026-03-14 60
summary
quit
```

prints

```
Added: 2026-03-14 09:00-10:30 Team meeting
Added: 2026-03-14 12:00-13:00 Lunch
Overlaps with Team meeting (09:00-10:30)
Saturday 2026-03-14
  09:00-10:30 Team meeting
  12:00-13:00 Lunch
Free: 08:00-09:00
2 events, 2h 30m planned
Busiest day: 2026-03-14 (2 events)
Bye.
```

**Event** is a record `Event(String title, LocalDateTime start, int minutes)` with `end()` and a method telling whether it overlaps another event (they overlap when each starts before the other ends; one ending exactly when the next starts is fine).

**Commands** (no prompts):

| Command | Output |
|---|---|
| `add` | `Added: <date> <HH:mm>-<HH:mm> <title>`, or `Overlaps with <title> (<HH:mm>-<HH:mm>)` naming the earliest-starting event it overlaps |
| `remove <title>` | Removes the earliest event with that title (ignoring case): `Removed: <title as stored>`, or `No event called <title>` |
| `day <date>` | The day name and date (`Saturday 2026-03-14`), then each event starting that day in time order as `  <HH:mm>-<HH:mm> <title>`, or `  Nothing planned.` |
| `free <date> <minutes>` | The earliest gap of at least that many minutes between 08:00 and 18:00 that day, as `Free: <HH:mm>-<HH:mm>` (the whole gap), or `No free slot of <minutes> minutes on <date>`. Any event overlapping the window counts, including its parts outside the window. |
| `summary` | `<n> events, <h>h <m>m planned` (`1 event` for one) and `Busiest day: <date> (<n> events)` (the earliest on a tie), or just `No events.` |
| invalid input | The `Invalid` message from `Command.parse` |
| `quit` | Ends the loop |

The program always ends by printing `Bye.`
hints: Write `Event` first and test `overlaps` in your head with touching events: 09:00-09:30 and 09:30-10:00 must not overlap.

For `freeSlot`, walk the sorted events that touch the 08:00-18:00 window with a "cursor" at the end of the busy time so far; the first gap between the cursor and the next event's start that is long enough is the answer, and the time after the last event is the final candidate.
A labelled loop (`loop: while (...)`) lets the `Quit` case leave the loop from inside the `switch`: `break loop;`.

The `java.time` methods you need: `start.plusMinutes(m)` for the end, `a.isBefore(b)` and `a.isAfter(b)` to compare, `dateTime.toLocalDate()` and `toLocalTime()` to split one apart (a `LocalTime` prints as `09:00`), `date.atTime(LocalTime.of(8, 0))` to join them, and `Duration.between(a, b).toMinutes()` for a gap. `date.getDayOfWeek()` gives `SATURDAY`; `getDisplayName(TextStyle.FULL, Locale.ENGLISH)` on it (from `java.time.format.TextStyle`) gives `Saturday`.
requirements: `Schedule` holds the rules (overlaps, removal, free-slot search, summary numbers) and knows nothing about input or output; `Main` only parses, calls `Schedule` and prints.
Use a `switch` over the sealed `Command` type, with no `default`.
Keep the events sorted by start time, and use `java.time` for all date and time work.
stretch: Add `week <date>`, which prints the seven days starting at that date with the number of events and planned hours for each.
